title: Feedback-loop must close the loop

facts.note: Scope gate: needs a parser reading the feature's kind field. This is the only gate; the source imposes no path or task-word restriction.
Retrieval hint only, not a gate: feature definitions commonly live here.
Retrieval hint only, not a gate.
Retrieval hint only, not a gate.
Validator finding: no SMOKE acceptance with a close_the_loop block containing consumer_reacted and drift_resolved.

fires: Planner authors or edits a feature with kind: feedback-loop that has no SMOKE acceptance at all.
A feedback-loop feature has a SMOKE acceptance but its close_the_loop block is missing, or lacks consumer_reacted or drift_resolved.

A feedback-loop feature's close_the_loop block lists both fields, but the acceptance only proves the producer emitted a correction (not that the consumer reacted and the predicate stops firing next cycle).
doesNotFire: Feature whose kind is anything other than feedback-loop.

Feedback-loop feature with at least one SMOKE acceptance whose close_the_loop block contains consumer_reacted and drift_resolved AND whose acceptance proves all three parts of success: correction emitted, consumer reacted, drift no longer fires next cycle.

given: A feature is marked kind: feedback-loop.
when: You author or revise its plan, WMBTs and acceptances.
then: Declare at least one SMOKE acceptance with a close_the_loop block containing both consumer_reacted and drift_resolved.
prefer: Follow the source example shape, e.g. acc:<wagon>:<wmbt_id>-SMOKE-NNN-close-the-loop with close_the_loop:{consumer_reacted, drift_resolved}.

Define success as all three: (a) producer detected a condition and emitted a correction, (b) consumer received and reacted (consumer_reacted), and (c) the producer's predicate no longer fires next cycle (drift_resolved).
avoid: Acceptances that stop at 'producer emitted a correction' without proving the consumer reacted.
Proving the consumer reacted without proving the drift is gone on the next cycle.
A close_the_loop block missing either required field, or placing it on a non-SMOKE acceptance.
why: A feedback loop only works if the correction is consumed and the triggering condition disappears; emission alone proves nothing about the loop closing.
evidence: The feedback-loop feature has ≥1 acceptance of SMOKE type whose close_the_loop block contains consumer_reacted and drift_resolved.
Validator planner.smoke.feedback-loop-close-the-loop reports no finding for the feature.
verifier_detail: Gate on feature kind == feedback-loop; otherwise not applicable.

Require at least one SMOKE acceptance carrying a close_the_loop block. Example (illustrative, not a required ID pattern): acc:<wagon>:<wmbt_id>-SMOKE-NNN-close-the-loop with close_the_loop:{consumer_reacted, drift_resolved}.
Term close_the_loop = the required SMOKE acceptance block for a feedback loop; required_fields: [consumer_reacted, drift_resolved]; both must be present.

Success semantics: (a) producer detected a condition and emitted a correction, (b) consumer received and reacted, AND (c) producer's predicate no longer fires next cycle (drift resolved). Field presence alone does not satisfy success if the acceptance proves only producer emission.
